claims.title: Joya de Ceren buried by ash
claims.summary: An eruption of the Laguna Caldera volcano seals the Maya farming village of Joya de Ceren under volcanic ash, preserving the daily life of ordinary agriculturalists in extraordinary detail.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-600-joya-de-ceren-buried-by-ash, claim TL:SLV:event:600:joya-de-ceren-buried-by-ash, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of Pipil Cuzcatlan
claims.summary: Nahua-speaking Pipil migrants establish the realm of Cuzcatlan, the Land of the Jewel, dominating the region west of the Lempa River with a society resembling that of the Aztecs.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1200-rise-of-pipil-cuzcatlan, claim TL:SLV:event:1200:rise-of-pipil-cuzcatlan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Joya de Ceren named World Heritage
claims.summary: UNESCO inscribes Joya de Ceren on the World Heritage List as a unique record of pre-Hispanic Maya farming life, the Pompeii of the Americas.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1993-joya-de-ceren-named-world-heritage, claim TL:SLV:event:1993:joya-de-ceren-named-world-heritage, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Alvarado's conquest begins
claims.summary: An expedition from Guatemala under Pedro de Alvarado enters the region, meeting fierce Pipil resistance west of the Lempa River as the Spanish conquest of the territory begins.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1524-alvarado-s-conquest-begins, claim TL:SLV:event:1524:alvarado-s-conquest-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: San Salvador permanently founded
claims.summary: After being abandoned and resettled several times in the face of Pipil resistance, the Spanish town of San Salvador is permanently established near the old Pipil capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1528-san-salvador-permanently-founded, claim TL:SLV:event:1528:san-salvador-permanently-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First cry of independence
claims.summary: An early uprising in San Salvador, associated with the priest Jose Matias Delgado, is suppressed but remembered as a first stirring of the independence movement.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1811-first-cry-of-independence, claim TL:SLV:event:1811:first-cry-of-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from Spain declared
claims.summary: The Act of Independence of Central America, signed in Guatemala City, frees the region including the province of San Salvador from Spanish rule.

claims.title: Federal Republic of Central America
claims.summary: The provinces adopt the constitution of the Federal Republic of Central America, a union of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica in which the Salvadoran Francisco Morazan becomes a leading figure.

claims.title: El Salvador becomes sovereign
claims.summary: As the federation dissolves amid civil war, El Salvador assumes fully sovereign powers as a separate republic and adopts its modern name.

claims.title: Communal lands abolished
claims.summary: Laws abolishing communal and Indigenous landholding open the highlands to coffee estates, dispossessing peasant communities and entrenching a landed oligarchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1881-communal-lands-abolished, claim TL:SLV:event:1881:communal-lands-abolished, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Uprising and la matanza
claims.summary: A peasant and Indigenous revolt in the coffee districts, linked to Farabundo Marti, is crushed by the army; in the ensuing repression, the matanza, estimates of those killed range from at least 10,000 to as many as 30,000.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1932-uprising-and-la-matanza, claim TL:SLV:event:1932:uprising-and-la-matanza, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Execution of Farabundo Marti
claims.summary: Agustin Farabundo Marti, the communist organiser of the uprising, is captured and executed by firing squad; his name is later taken by the FMLN guerrilla front.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1932-execution-of-farabundo-marti, claim TL:SLV:event:1932:execution-of-farabundo-marti, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hernandez Martinez seizes power
claims.summary: General Maximiliano Hernandez Martinez takes power in a coup, beginning his dictatorship and inaugurating nearly half a century of military rule allied with the oligarchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1931-hernandez-martinez-seizes-power, claim TL:SLV:event:1931:hernandez-martinez-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Archbishop Romero
claims.summary: Archbishop Oscar Romero is shot dead while celebrating Mass; the UN Truth Commission later concludes he was killed by a right-wing death squad, an act that helped ignite the war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1980-assassination-of-archbishop-romero, claim TL:SLV:event:1980:assassination-of-archbishop-romero, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: El Mozote massacre
claims.summary: An army counterinsurgency operation kills hundreds of villagers at El Mozote and nearby hamlets; in 2012 President Funes apologised for the deaths of 936 people.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1981-el-mozote-massacre, claim TL:SLV:event:1981:el-mozote-massacre, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Chapultepec Peace Accords
claims.summary: The government and the FMLN sign the UN-brokered Chapultepec Peace Accords in Mexico City, ending the civil war, reforming the armed forces and turning the FMLN into a political party.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-1992-chapultepec-peace-accords, claim TL:SLV:event:1992:chapultepec-peace-accords, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Truth Commission report
claims.summary: The UN Commission on the Truth for El Salvador issues its report, From Madness to Hope, documenting wartime atrocities in a conflict in which more than 75,000 people are estimated to have died.

claims.title: Dollarisation
claims.summary: El Salvador retires its national currency, the colon, and adopts the US dollar as legal tender, deepening ties to the United States economy and to migrant remittances.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-2001-dollarisation, claim TL:SLV:event:2001:dollarisation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bukele wins the presidency
claims.summary: Nayib Bukele, a former mayor of San Salvador, wins the presidency outside the FMLN and ARENA, ending decades of two-party dominance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-2019-bukele-wins-the-presidency, claim TL:SLV:event:2019:bukele-wins-the-presidency, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bitcoin made legal tender
claims.summary: El Salvador becomes the first country in the world to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender alongside the US dollar.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-2021-bitcoin-made-legal-tender, claim TL:SLV:event:2021:bitcoin-made-legal-tender, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: State of exception and gang crackdown
claims.summary: After a surge of gang killings, the government imposes a state of exception suspending constitutional protections and launches mass arrests; homicides fall sharply amid human-rights concerns over tens of thousands detained.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-2022-state-of-exception-and-gang-crackdown, claim TL:SLV:event:2022:state-of-exception-and-gang-crackdown, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bukele re-elected
claims.summary: Despite a constitutional ban on consecutive terms, cleared by a loyal court, Bukele is re-elected by a landslide of about 85 percent of the vote.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of El Salvador: From the Pipil land of Cuzcatlan and the ash-buried Maya village of Joya de Ceren to independence from Spain in 1821, a coffee republic ruled by an oligarchy, the slaughter of 1932, the civil war of 1980 to 1992, and the gang crackdown of the Bukele era.", terralore.co/country/SLV/chronicle#ev-2024-bukele-re-elected, claim TL:SLV:event:2024:bukele-re-elected, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
